:::{#about-block}

Hi! I’m Rasmus Puggaard-Rode, roughly pronounced [ˈʁɑsmus ˌpʰukːɒːˀˈʁoːɤ]. 
I am Associate Professor of Phonetics at the University of Oxford, based at the [phonetics lab](https://www.phon.ox.ac.uk/){target='_blank'}, and an Official Fellow of [Kellogg College](https://www.kellogg.ox.ac.uk/){target='_blank'}. 

My work combines corpus and experimental methods to untangle the many different ways categorical differences between speech sounds (especially consonants) can be realized phonetically, and what this means for the structure of language.
This work involves working with both well-described Nordic languages and under-resourced languages of [south-east Asia](https://www.isca-archive.org/speechprosody_2024/kirby24_speechprosody.html){target='_blank'} and [Australia](https://www.isca-archive.org/speechprosody_2024/jepson24_speechprosody.html){target='_blank'}. I also work on developing general-purpose tools and pipelines for [processing](https://github.com/rpuggaardrode/getVOT){target='_blank'}, [analyzing](https://github.com/kirbyj/praatsauce/tree/new-version){target='_blank'}, and [visualizing](https://rpuggaardrode.github.io/praatpicture_manual/){target='_blank'} speech data. 

I hold a PhD in phonology and phonetics from Leiden University. [My dissertation](https://www.lotpublications.nl/stop-hey-whats-that-sound){target='_blank'} deals the class of consonant sounds in Danish known as stops: how they are [phonetically](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wocn.2022.101191){target='_blank'} [realized](https://www.journal-labphon.org/article/id/6449/){target='_blank'}, how they are [structured in the grammar of the language](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03740463.2021.2022866){target="_blank"}, and how they [vary among speakers of different dialects](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0095447024000603){target='_blank'}. Before coming to Oxford, I was a postdoc in the [Spoken Language Processing group](https://www.en.phonetik.uni-muenchen.de/research/research_groups/speech_processing/index.html){target='_blank'} at the [Institute for Phonetics and Speech Processing, Ludwig Maximilian University](https://www.en.phonetik.uni-muenchen.de/index.html){target="_blank"}.

:::

<h2 style='text-align: center;'>News</h2>

* I will be at this year's [Colloquium of the British Association of Academic Phoneticians](https://sites.google.com/view/baap2026/home){target='_blank'} at the University of Warwick, where I'll be presenting collaborative work with [Francesco Burroni](https://sites.google.com/cornell.edu/francescoburroni/){target='_blank'} and [Aleese Block](https://www.en.phonetik.uni-muenchen.de/people/staff/block_aleese/index.html){target='_blank'} on the acoustic and articulatory outcome of /d/-vocalization in Danish. You can read the abstract [here](https://rasmuspuggaard.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/2026_baap.pdf){target='_blank'}. Hope to see you there!

* I have received a small research grant from the John Fell Oxford University Press Fund to investigate Danish /d/-vocalization in real and apparent time using the [LANCHART corpus](https://lanchart.hum.ku.dk/){target='_blank'}. This project will run over the next few years.

* [Katie Jepson](https://languages-cultures.uq.edu.au/profile/10666/kathleen-jepson){target='_blank'}, [John Mansfield](http://langwidj.org/wp/){target='_blank'} and I organized a successful special session on the [stylized sustained prosody](https://www.isca-archive.org/speechprosody_2024/jepson24_speechprosody.html){target='_blank'} pattern found in the narrative register of many native Australian languages at this year's [Australian Linguistic Society](https://als.asn.au/Conference/2025/General){target='_blank'} meeting. I couldn't go, but got to attend remotely from the home office. Thanks to everyone who contributed!

* I was recently in Copenhagen for a [symposium](https://lingvistkredsen.ku.dk/kalender/efteraar-2025/trends-in-phonology-fylder-50/){target='_blank'} celebrating the 50th anniversary of Eli Fischer-Jørgensen's classic monograph [*Trends in Phonological Theory*](https://lingvistkredsen.ku.dk/udgivelser/travaux/arkiv/tclc_27_proofread.pdf){target='_blank'}, where I gave an invited talk (in Danish) on what regional variation in Danish stop gradation can tell us about the relationship between phonetics and phonology. Slides are available [here](https://rasmuspuggaard.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/2025_trends.pdf){target='_blank'}.

* The proceedings from the third [International Conference on Tone and Intonation](https://www.tai2025.org/){target='_blank'} have been published. [Nicolai Pharao](https://nors.ku.dk/ansatte/?pure=da/persons/164799){target='_blank'} and I have a paper in this volume on what appears to be a specialized pitch accent used by some speakers of Danish for contrastive emphasis. You can read the paper [here](https://www.isca-archive.org/tai_2025/pharao25_tai.html){target='_blank'}.
